papers_read.title_as_printed: Class activation attention transfer neural networks for MCI conversion prediction (Luo, He, Cui, Chen, Ward; Computers in Biology and Medicine 156 (2023) 106700)
Early progression detection from MCI to AD using multi-view MRI for enhanced assisted living (Rahim et al., Image and Vision Computing 157 (2025) 105491)

what_each_reports.P-3: 593 ADNI-1/2 baseline MCI (295 pMCI diagnosed with dementia within 36 months, 298 sMCI), using the Wen et al. benchmark splits; whole 3D T1 MRI into a 5-layer 3D CNN with attention maps transferred from AD/CN, ADAS and CDR-SB source tasks (source pretraining on up to 1587 subjects); 5-fold CV. CAAT ensemble accuracy 74.61% (variance 0.002), SEN 0.75, SPE 0.75, AUC 0.780. The authors note that using 5-fold CV for both tuning and selection 'may lead to an optimistically biased evaluation'.
what_each_reports.P-41: 192 ADNI-1/GO/2 3 T subjects: 96 sMCI (MCI through M48) vs a positive class of 81 pMCI (converted between M18 and M48) plus 15 established AD patients; 132 2D slices per plane through a heterogeneous EfficientNet/ConvNeXt/DenseNet + CBAM + multi-head attention ensemble; test set 15 + 15 subjects. Accuracy 91.77 +/- 3.14%, SEN 87.69%, SPE 88.53%, AUC 92.87%.

quantity_a: Accuracy of pMCI (dementia within 36 months) vs sMCI (still MCI at 36 months), MCI only, from whole 3D T1 images, ADNI-1/2, 5-fold CV on 593 subjects.
quantity_b: Accuracy of 48-month-stable sMCI vs a positive class of M18-M48 converters plus established AD patients, from 2D multi-plane slices, ADNI 3 T, a single 30-subject held-out test.
incompatible_if_same: Not established. P-3 reports a small run-to-run variance around 74.61%, and P-41 reports +/-3.14 around 91.77% on 30 test subjects. These spreads are not intervals for one population quantity, and P-41's test classes differ in composition from P-3's.

gates.task: nominal match (T2), but P-41's positive class includes 15 already-demented AD patients (and pMCI is defined as conversion between M18 and M48), while P-3 uses pure MCI with a 36-month horizon.
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (ADNI-1/2 vs ADNI-1/GO/2); subject overlap is likely.
gates.validation_tier: match (both internal): 5-fold CV on 593 vs a 30-subject held-out test.
gates.modality_family: match on structural T1 MRI; the input representations differ (whole 3D volume vs 2D slice stacks from three planes).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both report accuracy, but the positive class of P-41 contains AD patients, which makes its task partly an AD-vs-MCI discrimination. The horizons also differ (36 months vs M18-M48 with M48 stability).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: P-41's 91.77% accuracy / 92.87% AUC are below 0.97 (small test set noted), and P-3 is well below.
independence: Both draw on ADNI T1 scans; overlapping MCI subjects are likely. Distinct author groups.
grounds: P-41 adds 15 established AD patients to its pMCI class, so its positive class is not the pMCI population of P-3; the populations behind the label differ.
The horizons differ: dementia within 36 months (P-3) vs conversion between M18 and M48 against stability to M48 (P-41).
The validation designs differ enough to change what the number estimates: 5-fold CV over 593 subjects on the Wen benchmark splits vs one 30-subject test set.
Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes: P-41's comparison table does not list P-3, and P-3 benchmarks only against methods re-implemented on its own splits.

evidence_quotes.quote: if a subject was diagnosed with Dementia within the following 36 months, he/she was grouped into pMCI; and if the patient’s diagnosis remained as MCI, we categorized him/her as sMCI.
Our dataset consists of 593 MRI images, consisting of 298 sMCIs and 295 pMCIs images. We performed 5 fold cross validation using the same data splits as that used in [11]
A limitation of our experimental setup is the use of 5 fold cross validation for both tuning and selecting the models. This may lead to an optimistically biased evaluation of the model performance.
Furthermore, we added 15 patients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously.

The MHA classifier in the same heterogeneous ensemble outperformed the LSTM with an accuracy of 91.77% ±3.14, sensitivity of 87.69% ±3.24, specificity of 88.53% ±3.53, and an impressive AUC of 92.87% ±3.58.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-41: Acc 91 on T2' omits that P-41's positive class includes 15 established AD patients and that the test set is 15 + 15 subjects.
The P-3 registry row's Sample_N_Approx '1587' is the source-task pretraining pool; the pMCI/sMCI sample is 593.
modality_family 'Neuroimaging' is a broad bucket; both papers are structural T1 MRI, but with different input representations (3D volume vs 2D slices).
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-41 result on MCI-only classes (AD patients excluded) with a 36-month horizon and a test set large enough for an interval excluding 74.61%. The paper does not report one.
